title: Cartesian System of Rectangular Co-ordinates
summary: The distance between P(x₁, y₁) and Q(x₂, y₂) is PQ = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]. It is used to test the type of a triangle: equal sides (isosceles or equilateral) and Pythagoras (right-angled).

The point dividing the join of (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) internally in the ratio m : n is ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m + n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m + n)). Externally, use m − n in place of m + n and −n in place of n. The midpoint is ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).
To find the ratio in which an axis divides a segment, take the ratio as k : 1 and set the other coordinate to zero. A negative k means external division.
Area = ½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|. Three points are collinear when this area is zero.

The centroid of a triangle is ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/3). The slope of the line joining two points is m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = tan θ, where θ is the angle the line makes with the positive x-axis.
mcq: The points A(−1, −1), B(2, 3) and C(−2, 6) are the vertices of —

mcq.work:
AB² = 3² + 4² = 25; BC² = 4² + 3² = 25; AC² = 1² + 7² = 50.
AB = BC and AB² + BC² = AC², so it is an isosceles right triangle.

mcq: The point P with ordinate −3 divides the join of A(6, 5) and B(−1, 4) in the ratio —

mcq.work:
Let the ratio be k : 1. y = (4k + 5)/(k + 1) = −3 ⇒ 4k + 5 = −3k − 3 ⇒ k = −8/7.
Negative k means external division in the ratio 8 : 7.

vsa: Find the ratio in which the line segment joining (2, −3) and (5, 6) is divided by the y-axis.

Let the ratio be k : 1. On the y-axis x = 0: (5k + 2)/(k + 1) = 0 ⇒ k = −2/5.
So the y-axis divides it externally in the ratio 2 : 5.
Find the area of the triangle whose vertices are (1, 2), (−2, 3) and (−3, −4).

Area = ½|1(2 − 5) + 5(5 + 1) + 9(−1 − 2)| = ½|−3 + 30 − 27| = 0.
The area is zero, so the points are collinear.
